result.summary: This PR makes bitcoind refuse to start when -listenonion is enabled and an explicit -bind is configured without a dedicated -bind=<addr>=onion. It updates several functional tests to use dedicated onion binds, adds a startup-time rejection with a clear error message in init.cpp, and documents the new requirement in a release note. It follows up on a recommendation made in the discussion of #34892.
result.problem: When Tor's automatic onion service shares a normal P2P bind, the node cannot tell Tor-forwarded connections from direct connections, so network classification (and any IP-based permissions like -whitelist noban) can be misapplied to Tor peers. This affects any operator running listenonion with an explicit -bind and no dedicated onion bind, which after this change requires action to keep starting.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp: wildcard onion binds (0.0.0.0:P=onion or [::]=onion) still pass the new check but classify peers by IP network and can retain whitelist permissions, defeating the purpose of the fix; asks if rejecting wildcards is in scope
jeanpablojp: doc/tor.md and the -bind help text ("default: 127.0.0.1:8334=onion") don't reflect the new requirement for setups with explicit -bind
jeanpablojp: nit that feature_bind_extra.py could use assert_start_raises_init_error instead of the manual FailedToStartError/re approach

result.card: This PR makes bitcoind refuse to start when Tor's automatic onion service would share a normal P2P bind, closing a gap where Tor-forwarded connections cannot be distinguished from direct connections and can silently inherit IP-based whitelist permissions. The problem affects any operator running -listenonion with an explicit -bind and no dedicated onion bind, a scenario the PR body ties to a recommendation from the closed PR #34892. Reviewer jeanpablojp gave a Concept ACK but also identified that wildcard onion binds (0.0.0.0 or [::]) still pass the new check while leaking the same permissions, asking if closing that gap is in scope; the author has not replied since 2026-09-04, over the 9-day waiting threshold. winterrdog gave an Approach ACK. The PR is currently Paused pending the author's response to that open scope question, though the core mechanism has no stated objections.
